extracted.intended_audience: scholarly_communication professionals (metadata managers, repository staff, publishers, librarians, Crossref staff), researchers interested in preprints and open peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and improving metadata records for preprints and open peer reviews, especially metadata that links preprints, peer reviews, and corresponding journal articles and that is exposed via Crossref. Focuses on availability, linking, and good metadata practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality metadata for preprints and open peer reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The increasing adoption of preprinting and of open or transparent peer review make it essential to have high-quality metadata for preprints and open peer reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality metadata is needed to optimally benefit from preprinting and open peer review; this is the overarching desideratum motivating the analysis and recommendations in the presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata linking preprints to corresponding journal articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata that links preprints to the corresponding journal articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presentation explores the availability of such preprint-article links in Crossref and presents detailed statistics on their availability; strong practice is to include explicit relation metadata that connects preprint records with their later journal versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata linking peer reviews to the items they review (journal articles or preprints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata that links peer reviews to the journal articles or preprints to which they pertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The talk examines links between peer reviews and the objects they review (both preprints and journal articles) and highlights the importance of these links for discoverability and provenance of reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of metadata in Crossref
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of metadata for preprints and open peer reviews, in particular metadata made available through Crossref.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors present detailed statistics showing how frequently Crossref contains preprint-article links and links between peer reviews and items; availability in Crossref is treated as a key measurable dimension of metadata quality and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of good metadata practices and remediation of shortcomings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of good metadata practices and identification of shortcomings in the metadata made available through Crossref, followed by recommendations for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presentation shows positive examples to model after and highlights shortcomings as anti-patterns; it concludes with recommendations aimed at improving metadata practices for preprints and open peer reviews (implying that metadata should be complete, explicit about relations, and exposed through community infrastructures like Crossref).
